full_target:
Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
\(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy

\[
[h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
\]

Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
\(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
\(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
\(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.

Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
\(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
algebraically closed.
conclusion: V_K is nonzero, and for every K-linear subspace W⊂V_K invariant under ρ_K(x⊗1), ρ_K(y⊗1), and ρ_K(h⊗1), either W={0} or W=V_K. Thus V(K) is irreducible as an L(K)-module, for every field K and every prime p and integer 0≤λ<p, including λ=0 and p=2.

hypotheses.statement: p is prime, K has characteristic p, and λ is an integer with 0≤λ<p.

V=V(λ) is the complex irreducible highest-weight sl₂(ℂ)-module of highest weight λ, has complex dimension λ+1, and its Chevalley generators x,y,h satisfy [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=−2y, [x,y]=h, both in sl₂(ℂ) and in their actions on V.
v∈V is nonzero, xv=0 and hv=λv.

M⊂V is an admissible lattice: it is a free abelian subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis of V, and it is stable under U_Z. The lattice is arbitrary; it is not assumed to be the minimal lattice.

definitions.definition: I={i∈ℤ:0≤i≤λ}; indices of finite sums and indexed families in this proof range over I unless another range is displayed.

definitions.type: family of elements of U(sl₂(ℂ)) and their induced operators on V, indexed by nonnegative integers
definitions.definition: For every integer r≥0, X(r)=X_r=x^r/r! in the complex universal enveloping algebra U(sl₂(ℂ)); the same notation denotes its action on V. Powers are compositions on V, with zeroth power the identity.

definitions.type: family of elements of U(sl₂(ℂ)) and their induced operators on V, indexed by nonnegative integers
definitions.definition: For every integer r≥0, Y(r)=Y_r=y^r/r! in U(sl₂(ℂ)); the same notation denotes its action on V, with zeroth power the identity.
U_Z is the unital ℤ-subalgebra of U(sl₂(ℂ)) generated by X(r) and Y(r) for all integers r≥0, acting on V by its given sl₂(ℂ)-representation.

definitions.type: p-local subring of ℚ, with its usual inclusion in ℂ
definitions.definition: R=ℤ_(p)={a/b∈ℚ:a,b∈ℤ, b≠0, p∤b}, with the operations inherited from ℚ and its usual embedding in ℂ.
M_R=R⊗_ℤ M. Its elementary tensors are written r⊗m with r∈R and m∈M.
ι_M(r⊗m)=r m, extending by addition from pure tensors, where R⊂ℂ and M⊂V. When its injectivity has been proved we identify M_R with its image under ι_M.
For i,j∈I, E_ij=E(i,j) is the unique complex-linear operator sending e_j to e_i and e_k to zero for each k∈I with k≠j.
Π=Y(λ)X(λ), with rightmost factor applied first.

definitions.type: family of R-submodules of ℂ indexed by I
definitions.definition: For i∈I, J_i={c∈ℂ:c e_i∈ι_M(M_R)}. Scalar operations are inherited from ℂ.
V_K=V(K)=M⊗_ℤ K, with K acting on the second tensor factor.

definitions.type: K-vector space obtained from the Chevalley integer form
definitions.definition: L_K=L(K)=(ℤx+ℤy+ℤh)⊗_ℤ K. The integer span uses the Chevalley generators in sl₂(ℂ) and its inherited bracket, and scalar extension gives the bracket on L_K.
For t∈ℤx+ℤy+ℤh, c,d∈K and m∈M, ρ_K(t⊗c)(m⊗d)=(tm)⊗(cd), extended additively and K-linearly. On V_K the words invariant under x,y,h mean invariant under ρ_K(x⊗1), ρ_K(y⊗1), ρ_K(h⊗1).
F_p=ℤ/pℤ, with residue classes of integers and quotient ring operations; its canonical map into K is [a]↦a·1_K.
